title: A Council That Learned to Listen

paragraphs.en: A university council once treated every quarrel about campus life as a problem of discipline. Students could chat in corridors, but formal meetings offered little opportunity to challenge a decision. When the university decided to appoint a student chair, Mara accepted only after asking the council to specify her responsibilities. She would supervise meetings, cooperate with staff, and help prescribe fair procedures, rather than simply endorse whatever the administration proposed. Some officials continued to assert that the old system worked. Mara asked them to refrain from judging the new arrangement before hearing those who had previously remained silent.
paragraphs.zh: 一所大学的委员会曾把校园生活中的每次争执都当成纪律问题。学生可以在走廊交谈，却很少能在正式会议中质疑决定。学校决定任命一位学生主席时，玛拉先要求委员会明确她的职责，才接受职位。她要主持会议、与教职工合作，并帮助制定公平程序，而不只是批准校方提出的任何建议。一些负责人仍坚持旧制度运转良好。玛拉请他们先听听过去沉默者的声音，再评价新的安排。

paragraphs.en: Her first test concerned a broken heating system. A resident agreed to testify about repeated complaints, although she did not dare identify the employee who had ignored them. Mara made a pledge to protect people from retaliation. She asked members not to yell across the room, but to collaborate in establishing the facts. Nobody needed to pronounce every technical term perfectly or utter an impressive speech. What mattered was whether anyone had tried to conceal a fault or deceive the residents. Students who chose to defy an unfair rule deserved a hearing; the chair would restrain personal attacks, not legitimate criticism.
paragraphs.zh: 她的第一次考验涉及损坏的供暖系统。一位住宿生同意说明自己反复投诉的经过，却不敢指认忽视投诉的工作人员。玛拉承诺保护大家不受报复。她要求与会者不要隔着会议室叫喊，而要共同查清事实。没有人需要把每个技术词都念得完美，也不必发表令人印象深刻的讲话。关键在于是否有人试图隐瞒故障或欺骗住户。选择反抗不公平规定的学生应当得到陈述机会；主席要制止的是人身攻击，而非合理批评。

paragraphs.en: The discussion revealed errors on both sides. An engineer asked residents to forgive an insulting reply, and Mara offered a compliment when he explained the repair clearly. Members began to practise a different style of debate: questions should enlighten the audience rather than hamper an opponent. The council could condemn careless conduct without humiliating a person. To mediate the dispute, Mara refused to proclaim an instant victory for either side. A transparent record would shield honest witnesses and help the agreement withstand later criticism. She would summon the parties again if the repairs failed, and invited the engineer to impart his knowledge to student volunteers.
paragraphs.zh: 讨论揭示了双方的错误。一位工程师请求住户原谅自己曾经无礼的回复；他清楚解释维修安排后，玛拉给予了肯定。委员们开始练习另一种辩论方式：提问应当帮助听众理解，而不是给对手设置障碍。委员会可以谴责不负责任的行为，却不必羞辱个人。为调解争端，玛拉拒绝立即宣布任何一方获胜。公开记录既能保护诚实的证人，也能让协议经得住日后的批评。若维修失败，她会再次召集双方，并请工程师向学生志愿者传授知识。

paragraphs.en: Changing the culture required more than a new chair. Senior members could still intimidate newcomers, who might then rebel against the entire process. A careless headline could amplify a rumor, so the council agreed to designate one person to publish verified minutes. Even an experienced speaker might stumble or allege something without evidence. Mara wanted public discourse to elicit information, not establish a reign of the loudest voices. She encouraged students to articulate concerns in their own language, sought counsel from quieter members, and promised to notify everyone of any revision. Before an important presentation, volunteers could rehearse together without having their opinions edited into obedience.
paragraphs.zh: 改变会议文化不只需要换一位主席。资深委员仍可能吓住新人，后者因而对整个程序产生抵触。草率的标题可能放大传言，于是委员会同意指定一人发布核实过的会议记录。即使经验丰富的发言者也可能表达失误，或提出没有证据的指控。玛拉希望公开讨论能够获取信息，而不是让嗓门最大的人统治会场。她鼓励学生用自己的语言说清担忧，向安静的委员征求意见，并承诺通知大家任何修订。重要汇报之前，志愿者可以一起排练，但不必为了服从而改掉自己的观点。

paragraphs.en: At the final meeting, students did not applaud every statement. One member began to exclaim that the council had solved everything, then stopped and corrected himself. No official could swear that future disputes would disappear. Yet the heating worked, complaints received answers, and the minutes explained who was responsible. Mara was happy to congratulate the volunteers, but her most useful decision was less dramatic: the council would convene regularly, including when there was no crisis. Trust grew because people could speak, question, and return, rather than because one polished speech persuaded them to remain quiet.
paragraphs.zh: 最后一次会议上，学生没有对每句话都鼓掌。有人兴奋地宣布委员会解决了一切，随后停下来纠正了自己。没有负责人能保证以后再无争端。但暖气恢复了，投诉得到答复，会议记录也说明了谁负有责任。玛拉高兴地祝贺志愿者，不过她最有价值的决定并不轰动：委员会将定期开会，即使没有危机也如此。信任的增长来自人们能够发言、追问、再度参与，而不是一篇漂亮讲话说服大家保持安静。
